shorts_extract.hook: Why stepping into a brand-new place triggers spine-tingling déjà vu—and why an MRI scanner proved it means your brain's fact-checker is sharp, not broken.
shorts_extract.core_experiment: Urquhart & Akira O'Connor (2021, St Andrews fMRI): missing-theme word lists triggered live déjà vu in 16 of 21 adults, lighting up frontal conflict-checkers while the hippocampus stayed quiet.
shorts_extract.twist: Without that frontal veto, you wouldn't feel eerie at all—you would blindly believe a false memory.
